summary.value: The Euskal Oiloa, or Basque hen, is the old farmyard chicken of the Basque Country in northern Spain. It is a hardy dual purpose bird of the Atlantic type, so unlike the Mediterranean breeds of Spain it has yellow legs, red earlobes and brown eggs. Roosters weigh about 8 pounds and hens about 5.5 pounds. Its single comb carries five to seven sharp points, and its skin is yellow. Five colors are recognized: black, red, golden cuckoo, black tailed white, and a red brown naked neck type. Hens lay roughly 209 to 220 brown eggs a year, each around 60 grams. Many males are raised as capons for the table. The breed lost ground to commercial brown egg hybrids, and a conservation program began in 1975. Spain approved its official standard in 2001 and lists it as a breed at risk.
